With clear skies and normal unaided vision, you should be able to spot it easily, assuming no buildings, trees, hills, or haze block that part of the eastern sky.

Look **low-ish in the east**, about 15° above the horizon—roughly **one and a half fist-widths at arm’s length**. It may appear slightly less than perfectly full, with the missing sliver on the **western/right-hand side** of the lunar disk as viewed in the sky, depending on its orientation.

The main caveats are local obstructions, thin haze near the horizon, and light pollution; none should prevent seeing such a bright, nearly full Moon if the eastern sky is reasonably open.
